metaDescription: Kakei Yamamoto is an MIT EECS PhD student working on inference, fine-tuning, generative models, machine learning theory, and optimization.

hero.heading: Kakei Yamamoto
hero.lead: PhD student in Computer Science at MIT, advised by Martin J. Wainwright. I work on inference, fine-tuning, generative models, machine learning theory, and optimization.
hero.affiliation: Research Assistant, Laboratory for Information & Decision Systems

bio.heading: Biography
paragraphs: I am a PhD student in Computer Science at MIT EECS and a research assistant at LIDS, advised by Martin J. Wainwright. I am also affiliated with IDSS.
My current research focuses on inference, fine-tuning, generative models, machine learning theory, and optimization, especially in settings involving distribution shift and model distillation.
Before MIT, I worked on deep learning theory at RIKEN AIP and studied Applied Mathematical and Computer Science at the University of Tokyo under Taiji Suzuki.

education.degree: BEng in Applied Mathematical and Computer Science

currentProjects.title: TILT
currentProjects.body: A current project studying how inference-time and fine-tuning procedures reshape model behavior in modern machine learning systems.

currentProjects.title: Implicit Importance Weighting
currentProjects.body: A one-step unsupervised domain adaptation method designed to avoid unstable density-ratio estimation while retaining the effect of relative density reweighting.

currentProjects.title: Residual-as-Teacher
currentProjects.body: A functional-gradient view of model distillation where learning from residuals mitigates teacher-bias propagation under high-dimensional covariate shift.

researchThemes.title: Inference and Fine-tuning
researchThemes.body: Studying adaptation and inference-time behavior in modern machine learning systems.

researchThemes.title: Distribution Shift
researchThemes.body: Understanding when learning systems can recover from biased or misspecified supervision, especially in student-teacher estimation.

researchThemes.title: Mean-Field Methods
researchThemes.body: Analyzing Langevin dynamics, policy gradients, and distributional minimax optimization in regimes where feature learning matters.

researchThemes.title: Generative Modeling
researchThemes.body: Studying conditional diffusion models, classifier-free guidance, and the mathematical structure behind generative sampling.

researchThemes.title: Neural Computation
researchThemes.body: Exploring timing-based learning and sparse-firing regularization for spiking neural networks and efficient inference.

publications.title: Implicit Importance Weighting for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
publications.summary: Develops a stable one-step alternative to explicit density-ratio estimation for domain adaptation under distribution shift.

publications.title: Residual-as-Teacher: Mitigating Bias Propagation in Student-Teacher Estimation
publications.summary: Proposes residual-as-teacher estimation to reduce teacher-bias propagation and proves excess-risk and convergence guarantees.

publications.title: Mean Field Langevin Actor-Critic: Faster Convergence and Global Optimality beyond Lazy Learning
publications.authors: Kakei Yamamoto, Kazusato Oko, Zhuoran Yang, Taiji Suzuki
publications.summary: Develops mean-field Langevin actor-critic methods for feature-learning policy optimization.

publications.title: Symmetric Mean-field Langevin Dynamics for Distributional Minimax Problems
publications.authors: Juno Kim, Kakei Yamamoto, Kazusato Oko, Zhuoran Yang, Taiji Suzuki
publications.summary: Extends mean-field Langevin dynamics to minimax optimization over probability distributions.

publications.title: Can Timing-Based Backpropagation Overcome Single-Spike Restrictions in Spiking Neural Networks?
publications.authors: Kakei Yamamoto, Yusuke Sakemi, Kazuyuki Aihara
publications.summary: Studies timing-based backpropagation beyond single-spike restrictions in spiking neural networks.

publications.title: Sparse-firing regularization methods for spiking neural networks with time-to-first-spike coding
publications.authors: Yusuke Sakemi, Kakei Yamamoto, Takeo Hosomi, Kazuyuki Aihara
publications.summary: Introduces spike-timing-based regularization methods to reduce firing frequency in TTFS-coded spiking neural networks.

works.title: BiteType! and BiteType! Classroom
